title: Agent Memory Benchmark adapter and submission
hypothesis: AutoMem can be evaluated against external AMB datasets by adapting benchmark memory and recall calls into the server's native API.
result: Adapter work exists with multiple LoCoMo, LongMemEval, PersonaMem, and BEAM runs, but the current long stability run is still active and no PR has been opened.
decision: Keep in progress until the active AMB run finishes, aggregate its outputs, and decide whether to PR the amb-adapter worktree.
notes: The active omb job runs from ../agent-memory-benchmark and writes to that repo's outputs directory; copy or summarize final AMB outputs here only after review.

title: Parallel matrix harness for AutoMem config sweeps
hypothesis: A matrix runner with isolated stacks can compare many endpoints, rulesets, and scenarios without cross-run contamination.
result: PR #19 merged the parallel matrix harness and supporting stack helpers.
decision: Adopted as infrastructure; no active worktree remains.
notes: Worktree reconciliation should report this branch as merged/cleanup-only if it appears again.

title: Native judged BEAM harness
hypothesis: AutoMem should be measured with BEAM's judged answer task, not only proxy retrieval metrics, to make leaderboard-comparable claims.
result: A native judged harness exists on the beam-judged branch with 100K results and an active longer stability run pending.
decision: Park promotion decisions until the active judged/AMB runs complete and the branch lands.
notes: This experiment is referenced before it lands on main; the first real index from main should be rerun after the branch merges.

title: BEAM retrieval proxy harness
hypothesis: A deterministic retrieval-only BEAM proxy can provide a cheap signal before running expensive judged BEAM.
result: PR #12 merged the retrieval proxy harness and documented the 100K proxy run.
decision: Use as a cheap preflight, not as the final benchmark claim.
notes: Retrieval proxy metrics should not be described as official BEAM scores.

title: BEAM mem0-shim harness
hypothesis: The upstream BEAM runner can be pointed at AutoMem through a mem0-compatible shim.
result: The shim established a baseline and revealed failure modes, but was replaced for ongoing work by retrieval proxy and native judged harnesses.
decision: Superseded by EXP-BEAM-RETRIEVAL and EXP-BEAM-JUDGED; keep artifacts for historical comparison.
notes: Use for historical failure analysis only.

title: Ruleset knob isolation and v2 defaults
hypothesis: Isolating recall knobs across the same scenarios can attribute quality changes to specific parameters.
result: The v2 default ruleset improved recall by combining wider time windows, higher limits, auto decomposition, and project tag gating.
decision: Adopt bare_tag_1m_v2 as the recommended local default; treat server-side expand_relations under tag gating as ineffective.
notes: compare_rulesets.py is still markdown-only; adding a JSON sidecar remains a later enhancement.

title: Production corpus stage-1 cleanup
hypothesis: Noisy memory clusters can be identified and staged for deletion without damaging preserved recall scenarios.
result: Stage-1 cleanup harness and reports were produced and PR #3 merged.
decision: Adopt staged cleanup workflow for raw corpus pruning.
notes: Preserve vs cleanup groups are useful vocabulary for later dashboards.

title: Layer-1 hook replay harness
hypothesis: Canned hook fixtures can detect capture-quality regressions before they reach production memory.
result: Hook replay, metrics, and diff tooling merged in PR #2 and follow-up hook field variants.
decision: Adopt as layer-1 regression coverage for ingestion hooks.
notes: This is operational regression tooling rather than benchmark scoring.

title: Current-state and temporal recall probes
hypothesis: Recall should prefer current facts over stale superseded facts when both exist.
result: Current-state fixture runner and PR #170 comparison reports were produced.
decision: Use as a targeted regression harness for temporal validity.
notes: Useful status fields include current_only, expectation, and probes passed.

title: Entity tag repair on real data
hypothesis: Canonicalizing entity tags and rejecting unsafe metadata updates can improve recall without broad overfetch.
result: Entity-repair harnesses and multiple fresh/loop runs were documented and merged in PR #8.
decision: Adopt staged repair evaluation before metadata migrations.
notes: Key variants include sync-only, reject-only, canonicalize-safe, and post-migration.

title: Server-side metadata signal diagnosis
hypothesis: Better metadata treatment can improve /recall behavior on real-data probes without changing vectors.
result: Worktree-safe metadata A/B tooling and server-side metadata search evals merged in PR #9 and PR #10.
decision: Adopt metadata A/B and vector identity checks as part of server-side recall diagnostics.
notes: Endpoint comparison has structured summary.json under sweep_runs, but markdown reports are separate.

title: Negative-control recall probes
hypothesis: Negative controls can expose broad overfetch and unsafe recall wins that positive-only scenarios miss.
result: Negative-control probes were added and documented in PR #11.
decision: Adopt as guardrail coverage for recall regression testing.
notes: Treat negative controls as safety checks, not quality wins.

title: WRIT adapter diagnostics
hypothesis: WRIT-style history-aware adapter diagnostics can complement /recall scenario scoring.
result: WRIT integration and adapter reporting merged in PR #6.
decision: Keep as a supplemental benchmark harness, separate from official AutoMem benchmark claims.
notes: third_party/writ may show submodule-local generated files during runs.

title: Memory maturation evaluation concept
hypothesis: Recall quality may improve through maturation or consolidation processes beyond immediate ingestion.
result: Design notes exist, but there is no durable runner or decision record yet.
decision: Parked until a concrete maturation runner is prioritized.

title: Undocumented FAMA, Memora, and relation-chain result clusters
hypothesis: These result clusters likely represent real experiments, but the hypothesis and decision are not recorded in session notes.
result: Artifact directories exist without a matching narrative writeup.
decision: Keep parked until someone reviews the raw outputs and either backfills records or deletes the artifacts.
notes: This placeholder keeps the clusters visible even though their scientific story still needs backfill.
